operational_definition: For each predicted non-null field, the system preserves an auditable link to the exact source evidence that supports that field value and its entity association (for example a passage, DOM element/path, stable attribute, table cell, screenshot region, or equivalent locator), not merely a record/page-level citation.
yes_rule: YES only when provenance is produced at field/value granularity and is evaluated or verifiably demonstrated for the system output.
partial_rule: PARTIAL when citations/URLs are attached only at answer, record, page, or document level; only a subset of fields is linked; or provenance is stored but not checked for value support/association.
no_rule: NO when outputs have no source linkage or only trajectory/navigation logs with no value-to-source binding.
nr_rule: NR when the paper does not report enough information to determine provenance granularity.
minimum_evidence: Architecture/output schema plus evaluation/examples showing field/value-to-source linkage; preferably a field-level provenance metric or explicit verification.
common_nonqualifiers: Record-level URL; answer citations; browser history; source list without per-field association; generic claim that output is grounded.
g1_use: A G1 system receives provenance=YES only under this rule; record-level citation is insufficient.

operational_definition: The evaluated system constructs a multi-record dataset over a declared collection boundary and handles the operations needed to make that dataset coherent: coverage/completeness of qualifying items, record construction, normalization, duplicate/entity reconciliation, missingness/conflicts, and final dataset output.
yes_rule: YES only when the system goes beyond isolated page/record extraction and the evaluation demonstrates dataset-level collection/assembly against a declared boundary or gold set.
partial_rule: PARTIAL when multiple structured records are produced but completeness, deduplication/entity reconciliation, or collection-boundary coverage is not evaluated; or the system assumes already-acquired data.
no_rule: NO for single-answer, single-record, page-local extraction, or data-preparation-only systems that do not perform collection/assembly.
nr_rule: NR when the paper describes structured outputs but does not specify whether dataset-level assembly/coverage occurs.
minimum_evidence: Declared collection boundary or dataset target; multi-record output; evidence of coverage/completeness and at least explicit normalization/dedup/entity-handling behavior.
common_nonqualifiers: Returning JSON for one page; extracting top-k without a declared boundary; cleaning a pre-existing table; narrative aggregation.
g1_use: Dataset assembly=YES requires end-to-end collection and coherent multi-record output; structured extraction alone is insufficient.

operational_definition: The same agent/policy/extraction method is evaluated on held-out or previously unseen websites/site families without site-specific redevelopment, retraining, selector engineering, or manual per-site adaptation after the test sites are known.
yes_rule: YES when the evaluation explicitly holds out websites/site families (or equivalent unseen-site split) and applies the same method without per-site redevelopment.
partial_rule: PARTIAL when several websites are used but all are seen during development/training; only new pages/layouts within the same site are tested; or limited few-shot/site-specific adaptation is required.
no_rule: NO when the method is site/template-specific; requires a new wrapper/script/selector per site; or is evaluated on one site only.
nr_rule: NR when multiple sites are mentioned but train/development/test site exposure and adaptation requirements are unclear.
minimum_evidence: Explicit unseen-site/domain split or documented deployment to new sites plus a statement that the same policy/method is reused without site-specific redevelopment.
common_nonqualifiers: Multi-site training alone; within-site page generalization; cross-task transfer on the same site; hand-written site adapters.
g1_use: Cross-site transfer is stricter than merely supporting many sites.

operational_definition: The required capabilities are demonstrated on the same end-to-end system under a common experimental pipeline/task set, so the evidence shows that the capabilities coexist in one evaluated system rather than being assembled across different papers, modules, benchmarks, or hypothetical architecture components.
yes_rule: YES only when the same system/run family is evaluated for every requirement needed by the claim with evidence attributable to the same end-to-end implementation.
partial_rule: PARTIAL when several requirements are evaluated on the same system but one or more are missing; or different benchmark tracks test disjoint subsets without showing they coexist in one end-to-end pipeline.
no_rule: NO when the conclusion is constructed by combining capabilities from separate systems/papers or when a conceptual architecture is not evaluated end to end.
nr_rule: NR when it is unclear whether reported modules/results belong to the same executable system configuration.
minimum_evidence: One identifiable system configuration plus results/artefacts covering every required dimension under the same implementation.
common_nonqualifiers: Literature synthesis across systems; separate ablations that never coexist; one paper citing another component; architecture diagram without end-to-end evaluation.
g1_use: The C1-11 universal absence claim can be retained only if no candidate system has all G1 requirement cells YES and joint_evaluation=YES.

operational_definition: The agent can discover and traverse a website or site state not encoded through a site-specific action script/wrapper using general observations/actions to reach relevant content under a high-level task.
yes_rule: YES when interactive navigation is executed on unseen or non-site-engineered Web environments and the agent selects actions dynamically.
partial_rule: PARTIAL for fixed benchmark sites known during development; replay/offline next-action prediction; or systems with substantial site-specific scaffolding.
no_rule: NO for static HTML extraction without navigation or site-specific wrappers that encode the navigation path.
nr_rule: NR when the paper does not describe whether navigation is dynamic or site-specific.
minimum_evidence: Executable browser/site interaction plus evidence that action selection is not a hard-coded site path.
common_nonqualifiers: Parsing already-downloaded HTML; offline element prediction only; fixed scraper traversal.
g1_use: Separate from cross-site transfer: a system may navigate dynamically on known sites yet fail held-out site transfer.

operational_definition: A machine-readable target schema or equivalent explicit field set/constraints is a first-class input/state/output contract and the system tracks or evaluates whether required fields/records are covered.
yes_rule: YES when schema fields/constraints directly govern extraction and coverage/completeness is evaluated or explicitly tracked.
partial_rule: PARTIAL for fixed JSON formats; templates; or task-specific output keys without coverage tracking or a general schema input.
no_rule: NO for free-form answers/reports or extraction whose target fields are implicit.
nr_rule: NR when structured output exists but the role of a schema/field contract is unclear.
minimum_evidence: Schema/field specification in the method plus field/record completeness or coverage behavior.
common_nonqualifiers: JSON syntax alone; answer-format markers; fixed benchmark labels with no schema-guided planning/extraction.
g1_use: Schema coverage requires more than syntactic structured output.

operational_definition: The system has an explicit mechanism that prevents flags abstains from nulls or penalizes predicted field values that are not supported by source evidence or the declared schema and this behavior is evaluated or verifiably demonstrated.
yes_rule: YES when unsupported non-null values are explicitly detected/penalized/blocked and the behavior is evaluated.
partial_rule: PARTIAL for generic hallucination mitigation reflection or confidence scoring without field-specific source/schema support checks.
no_rule: NO when the system can emit structured values without an explicit unsupported-value check.
nr_rule: NR when verification is claimed but the handling of unsupported fields is unspecified.
minimum_evidence: Field-level source/schema verification plus explicit abstention/null/penalty/rejection behavior.
common_nonqualifiers: Generic self-reflection; record-level citation; post-hoc narrative fact checking; schema validation that checks type but not source support.
g1_use: This is the negative-control complement to field-level provenance: a source link alone is not sufficient if unsupported values are not rejected.
